definitions.explanation: The number 100,000, formed as {十|じゅう} (ten) × {万|まん} (10,000). English switches unit here — "hundred thousand" — while Japanese simply counts ten {万|まん}.

examples.japanese: {十万|じゅうまん}{円|えん}の{時計|とけい}。
その{動画|どうが}は{十万|じゅうまん}{回|かい}{再生|さいせい}された。
examples.english: That video was viewed a hundred thousand times.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で、{十万|じゅうまん}{世帯|せたい}{以上|いじょう}が{停電|ていでん}した。
examples.english: Because of the typhoon, more than a hundred thousand households lost power.

notes:
Because Japanese groups digits in fours and English in threes, this is the point where mental conversion becomes error-prone: 100,000 is {十万|じゅうまん} (ten {万|まん}), and 1,000,000 is {百万|ひゃくまん} (a hundred {万|まん}).

CONVERSION LANDMARKS:
- {一万|いちまん}: 10,000
- {十万|じゅうまん}: 100,000
- {百万|ひゃくまん}: 1,000,000
- {一億|いちおく}: 100,000,000

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {十万|じゅうまん}{円|えん}: one hundred thousand yen
- {十万|じゅうまん}{人|にん}: one hundred thousand people
- {十万|じゅうまん}{回|かい}: a hundred thousand times
